prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Charlotte after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Charlotte for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you a tailored list, but first: do you want me to look up current Charlotte-area personal-injury firms and give phone numbers and short notes (I can pull 5–7 good options)? I can do that now if you want up-to-date contact details.

If you want a quick, actionable start without a web search, call 3–5 firms that cover these types of practices (below I give one large national option I’m sure has a Charlotte office plus guidance on the other types to call and why):

1) Morgan & Morgan — why call:
- National plaintiff firm with a Charlotte office that handles a high volume of car-accident cases on contingency.
- Experience with serious injuries, insurance-company negotiations, and litigation if necessary.
- Usually offers free consultation and takes cases on contingency (they advance costs).

2) Local plaintiff-focused boutique firms — why call:
- Often provide more personalized attention, local knowledge of Mecklenburg County judges and courts, and attorneys who focus exclusively on car-accident/personal-injury work.
- Good for cases where you want close attorney contact and a lawyer who will handle the file personally.

3) Small plaintiff-only trial firms with strong courtroom experience — why call:
- If fault or damages are disputed, a firm that tries cases frequently can be more effective in maximizing settlements or winning at trial.
- They’ll usually have trial results and verdicts to show.

4) Firms that handle serious/complex injuries (catastrophic injury, spinal cord, brain injury) — why call:
- These firms have medical experts, life-care planners, and resources to value long-term care and future damages.
- Important if your injuries are severe or will require ongoing care.

How many firms to call and what to ask when you call
- Call 3–5 firms: 1 national, 1–2 local boutiques, and 1 trial-focused firm (or one that advertises catastrophic-injury experience).
- Questions to ask on the initial call:
  - Do you take car-accident cases on contingency? (what % and are there any upfront costs?)
  - Do you offer a free consultation?
  - Who will actually handle my case (name of attorney/assistant)?
  - What’s your experience with cases like mine (injury type, seat-belt use, uninsured/underinsured motorist, intersection crashes)?
  - Do you have trial experience and recent verdicts/settlements you can share?
  - How do you handle medical liens and treatment costs while the case is ongoing?
  - Typical timeline and communication frequency (how often you’ll hear updates)?
  - Do you perform independent accident investigation (reconstructors, evidence preservation)?

What to have ready when you call
- Police report number (or copy), date/time/location of crash
- Photos of the crash/vehicle damage/injuries
- Health care providers and bills/records for treatment so far
- Insurance information (yours and the other driver’s)
- Any witness contacts or dashcam footage

If you want, I’ll now:
- Search and produce 5–7 specific, current Charlotte personal-injury law firms with phone numbers, websites, short notes on strengths, and a suggested order to call them. Want me to do that?
